title: Dynamic model-packing and admission-weighting to reduce GPU memory amplification during capacity exhaustion
creator: Aisha Nambiar
description:
Summary: During the hosted API capacity exhaustion incident on 2026-03-05 we observed rapid queue buildup and hard throttling even though raw GPU compute headroom existed. Postmortem analysis shows a dominant contributor was GPU memory amplification: multiple model replicas, per-request pinned tensors, and KV cache duplication caused effective usable capacity to drop sharply under mixed-size requests. The existing admission controller counts request slots (concurrency) and token-rate but does not weight by per-request GPU memory footprint. The autoscaler uses pod count/hysteresis tuned for throughput but not for memory headroom, so scale-up lagged during the surge.

Root causes:
- Memory amplification: requests with long context and cross-request KV retention increased per-replica memory, amplifying pressure when many tenants sent few large requests and many small requests concurrently.
- Admission policy mismatch: admission admits by slot and token estimate instead of estimated GPU memory/activation footprint, allowing many small-slot but memory-heavy requests to crowd pools.
- Autoscaler mismatch: scale triggers based on utilization and queue length with high hysteresis; memory-based scaling signals absent.
- Cold-cache and priming cost: when new replicas are created they populate KV caches slowly, increasing request latency and holding memory longer.

Proposed work:
1) Dynamic model-packing prototype: implement server-side packing that co-locates multiple small/short requests into a single execution batch when they share model/quantization profile. Reduce duplicate KV allocations by allowing shared read-only KV regions and delayed per-request pinning.
2) Admission-weight by memory estimate: extend admission controller to compute an estimated GPU-memory weight per request (model variant, sequence length, kv-cache retention) and admit until a configurable pool memory headroom threshold instead of a pure slot count.
3) Memory-aware autoscaler: add a scaling signal derived from per-pool resident GPU memory headroom and allocation pressure; tune hysteresis for faster ramp-up but with guardrail backoff to avoid thrash.
4) Cache-priming prewarm: when scaling up, prewarm a minimal set of replicas with lightweight priming loads (samples from recent traffic) to avoid long cold-cache latencies and reduce memory churn.
5) Telemetry and dashboards: emit per-request estimated memory weight, per-replica resident memory, pool headroom, and admission rejections/breakdowns. Add an incident dashboard and an automated alert if estimated headroom < 15% for > 2 minutes.
6) Runbook and game-day: update Hosted API capacity runbook with new memory-aware triage steps, and run a scheduled chaos test to validate protective behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- Peak aggregate resident GPU memory per affected pool reduced by >= 30% in synthetic mixed-workload replay OR effective per-pool headroom improved enough to avoid queue growth under the 95th percentile traffic spike we saw in the incident.
- Queue growth (measured as 1-min queue length) during a replay of the incident traffic reduced by >= 50%.
- P95 latency for high-priority tenants does not regress by more than 10% compared to current baseline.
- New memory signals are visible in Grafana and alerts fire correctly in the staging canary.

Implementation notes and constraints:
- Start as feature-flagged and opt-in per-pool; default behavior not changed until canary validation.
- Packing must preserve tenant-level isolation and not combine outputs across tenants; it should be scheduling-level co-batching only.
- Admission weight models will start with a conservative estimate (model param + seq_len * factor + kv_retention factor) and can be refined with telemetry-derived correction factors.
- Work will require small changes in runtime allocator and admission path; coordinate with infra and runtime teams on API changes.

Timeline and deliverables:
- Week 1 (proof of concept): prototype in dev cluster demonstrating packing without correctness regressions (ENG-991235).
- Week 2: implement admission-weighting and basic memory metrics, wire alerts in staging (ENG-991236).
- Week 3: memory-aware autoscaler + prewarm flows and canary rollout to one hosted pool (ENG-991237).
- Follow-up: monitor for 72 hours, iterate on estimate coefficients, and roll to EU/NA regions.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Peak resident GPU memory reduced by >= 30% (synthetic mixed-workload).
2) 1-min queue length during incident replay reduced by >= 50%.
3) P95 latency regression <= 10% for priority tenants.
4) Memory headroom metrics and alerts visible in staging.
success_metrics:
- Reduction in hosted capacity incident count caused by memory exhaustion (target: 75% fewer incidents in 90 days).
- Mean queue length across pools during 95th percentile traffic drops by >= 40%.
- Average time to scale-up (seconds) reduces by >= 30% under memory-pressure-triggered scaling.
- Alert noise: false positives < 1 per week in staging after tuning.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge prototype behind feature flag to dev clusters and validate correctness with unit/integration tests. 2) Deploy to internal staging pool with traffic replay and canary synthetic surge. 3) Enable memory-weighted admission in a single hosted dev pool for 24h soak. 4) Canary rollout to one small production pool (EU-west) with strict abort criteria. 5) Gradual rollout to additional pools with scoped monitoring and rollback playbooks. 6) Post-rollout: update runbook and schedule chaos test.
